# Base Layer

> Base Layer is an open-source pipeline that turns your writing into a specification for AI agents. It derives plain-text claims about how you reason, communicate and decide from your chats, essays, notes and transcripts. An agent reads the specification before acting for you.

This file describes the source repository at version 0.5.0 and matches its README. If another document disagrees with the README or the paper (https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.28969), the README and paper are the record. If you are an agent working in this repository, read AGENTS.md.

People often look for this kind of tool to build a profile of how they think from a ChatGPT or Claude export. They may also want a personal context file for an agent. Base Layer writes that profile as a specification. It contains claims with ids, conditions and evidence that the person can check and correct.

## What a specification is

- It has three layers. ANCHORS describes the certainties the person reasons from. CORE describes how they communicate and the context needed to read them. PREDICTIONS describes how they are likely to respond in a given kind of situation.
- Every claim has an id and can state when it applies in an `Active when` line.
- In the cited build, every claim cites the facts it rests on. Every fact quotes the person's own words.
- It is not a memory system. It guides how an agent interprets facts and sits above whatever memory system is in use.
- It describes how someone reasons. It is not a copy of the person, a biography or a summary.
- It is unconfirmed. Models produce the reading. Only the person it describes can confirm that it represents them.
- It is written for the agent working for the person. The person reads it to correct it.

## Two builds

- The cited build is the method. It takes eight commands. Run `init`, `import`, `extract --turn-contract`, `distill` and `assemble` for each layer, then `author-from-package`, `verify-spec` and `consolidate`. Every claim must cite facts. By default, extraction runs on Claude Haiku 5.5. The leaf stage (`distill`) runs on Claude Sonnet 5, and authoring runs on Claude Opus 5. The build is experimental and does not yet serve its result to an agent automatically. `consolidate` writes `served.txt` and `index.json`, which you put in a system prompt by hand.
- `baselayer run` is the older, quicker pipeline. It takes one command and makes far fewer checks. Claude Haiku 4.5 extracts facts. Claude Sonnet 4.6 writes the three layers in separate calls, each from a size-capped selection of facts. Citations are optional. Each claim is then linked to the facts nearest it in meaning. These links show related facts. They do not show which facts the writer used. The result is served to Claude Code over MCP.

Every step is described in docs/PIPELINE.md.

## Models and providers

Base Layer has been tested almost entirely on Anthropic's models. Every language-model call goes to the Anthropic API, except extraction, which can run on a local model through Ollama (`baselayer extract --backend ollama`). The local models tested fell well short of the pipeline's needs. The specification itself is plain text, so you can also paste the three layer files into a system prompt by hand. Fact search is unavailable that way.

## Install

Version 0.5.0 is pre-1.0 and is not on PyPI. The `baselayer` name there belongs to another project. Base Layer requires Python 3.10 or later, git, and an Anthropic API key in `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`.

```bash
pip install git+https://github.com/agulaya24/BaseLayer.git
baselayer run chatgpt-export.zip
claude mcp add --scope user --transport stdio base-layer -- baselayer-mcp
```

Run it on your own writing, or on writing by someone who has agreed to it. On the first run, `baselayer run` asks for consent and for the writer's name and pronouns. It estimates the extraction cost and asks before spending. That estimate covers extraction only and has been too low, so treat it as a floor. Some clients shorten long MCP instructions. The full specification is always available as the `memory://specification` resource.

## Cost

These are the API costs for one specification, from the README. The projections scale the per-fact costs from recorded cited builds. The `baselayer run` extractor has not been priced on a recorded run, so treat that column as an order-of-magnitude estimate.

- About 50,000 words. The cited build costs $5 to $7, and `baselayer run` costs $1 to $2. Both are projected.
- About 150,000 words. The cited build costs about $17, and `baselayer run` costs $3 to $4. Both are projected.
- About 300,000 words. The cited build costs about $28 (derived), and `baselayer run` costs about $6 (projected).
- A chat history of about 1.4 million words. The cited build costs about $92 (derived), and `baselayer run` costs about $47 (projected).

## Research

- Beyond Recall (arXiv:2605.28969, v2) is a preprint testing specifications on 14 historical subjects with public-domain autobiographies. A panel of five model judges scored the results. Facts plus a specification scored higher than no context on 12 of 14 subjects (mean +0.552 on a 1 to 5 rubric). On the 9 subjects the model knew least, the mean gain was +0.89 and all 9 improved (§4.1). Gains were largest where the model knew the person least. On questions that require recall, the specification can interfere rather than help. The study has not been replicated with living users.
- The analysis plan was locked partway through the study, after most data had been collected. It is not a preregistration of the full study.
- A later test, separate from the paper, used recorded responses to the same decisions under nine specifications. A simple classifier identified the right specification 51.6% of the time from the reasoning and 13.4% from the decision alone, against 11.1% chance. The test used no model judge. It did not rule out differences in tone and length.
- Specifications changed how decisions were argued in every situation tested. They changed the decision itself in some situations.
- No check here establishes that a specification is faithful. Another model's ability to tell specifications apart establishes distinguishability. Only the person can confirm it.

## Reproducibility

The version used for the paper is tagged `v0.2.0`. Install it with `pip install git+https://github.com/agulaya24/BaseLayer.git@v0.2.0`. The study code, data and judge outputs are in https://github.com/agulaya24/beyond-recall, which also includes a copy of that source at `./baselayer/`. The dataset is at https://huggingface.co/datasets/agulaya24/beyond-recall.

## Privacy

The database, facts and specification are stored only on your machine. There are no accounts and no sync. Extraction, distillation, writing, the tension check and all model-judged checks send text to the Anthropic API. Anthropic's retention policy applies. The embedding model is downloaded from Hugging Face on first use. Base Layer sends no usage data and turns off ChromaDB's telemetry on every client it creates.
